collar_tag_req: Every licence issued pursuant to this by-law shall be in the form of a cat or dog tag. When a cat or dog is off the property of the Owner or Guardian the Owner or Guardian shall cause the cat or dog to wear around the neck a collar to which shall be attached the current licence tag issued for that cat or dog by the municipality.
dog_limit: A maximum limit applies: no person shall keep more than 4 dogs on the premises of a single family dwelling. If there are multiple dwelling units on the parcel of land, no person shall keep more than 2 dogs per dwelling unit. Registered breeders are exempt from these limits.
notes: URL: https://cdnsm5-hosted.civiclive.com/UserFiles/Servers/Server_11976345/File/Our%20Services/Enforcement%20Services/By-Laws/By-Law%202021-8593%20Licencing,%20Registration,%20Regulation%20and%20Control%20of%20Cats%20and%20Dogs.pdf. The bylaw defines a 'Domestic Animal' to include animals kept as a 'work animal', but there are no specific definitions or exemptions for farm dogs, herding dogs, or LGDs. Barking is governed by a strict Noise Evidence Procedure without agricultural exemptions.

collar_tag_req: The Owner of every Dog having obtained a Licence and Tag for each Dog, as required by this By-law shall keep the Tag securely fixed at all times on the Dog for which the Tag was issued.
dog_limit: A maximum of three (3) dogs is permitted per residence. Keeping more than the prescribed number requires a valid Kennel licence.
notes: URL: https://www.vaughan.ca/sites/default/files/2023-03/066-2020%20%28Consolidated%29.pdf. Standard urban-focused animal control by-law. No working dog or LGD provisions found. Barking is restricted under a separate noise control by-law (121-2021) with no agricultural exemptions for dogs.

collar_tag_req: All dogs living in the Township of Uxbridge must be licensed and wear the tag on their collar.
dog_limit: A maximum of two (2) dogs per dwelling is permitted. However, the Township allows a third dog if the owner is on lands zoned (RU) RURAL as per Zoning By-law 81-19 and the parcel is larger than four (4) hectares in size.
notes: URL: https://uxbridge.docupet.com/en_CA/licensing. Animal control services for Uxbridge are provided by the shared Uxbridge-Scugog Animal Control Centre. The full text of the animal control by-law is not available online, but the Township's pet licensing portal outlines the rules. The Township uniquely extends the household dog limit (+1 extra dog) specifically for large rural and agricultural properties.

collar_tag_req: No owner shall keep any dog in the Township of Wainfleet unless such dog has on a collar on which is affixed a dog tag issued under the provisions of this by-law. The owner shall keep the dog tag securely fixed on the dog at all times until the dog tag is renewed or replaced.
dog_limit: A limit of 3 dogs applies per household unless a kennel licence is obtained.
notes: URL: https://www.wainfleet.ca/media/504. Standard animal control by-law. The Ontario Sheep Farmers submitted a proposal in 2022 requesting the addition of LGD/Herding Dog definitions and dog limit exemptions for agricultural properties, but current online by-laws do not yet reflect these updates. Barking dogs are governed by Noise Control By-law (028-2022) which explicitly exempts Agricultural Operations.

collar_tag_req: On payment of the license fee, the owner shall be furnished with a dog tag bearing a serial number. The owner shall keep the tag securely fixed on the dog at all times until the tag is renewed or replaced, except while the dog is being lawfully used for hunting in the bush.
dog_limit: A maximum of 3 dogs per property applies before kennel rules and zoning regulations take effect.
notes: URL: https://www.westgrey.com/media/nskibzsk/dog-licencing-bylaw-087-2009.pdf. While the Dog By-law itself lacks specific LGD definitions, the Township's new Noise Bylaw (2025-100) is highly farm-friendly. It explicitly restricts persistent barking by domestic pets but completely exempts animals 'kept or used for any purpose other than agriculture, provided that the agricultural use is permitted under the Municipality's Zoning Bylaw'.

collar_tag_req: Every owner of a cat or dog shall at the time of licensing the animal, pay an animal licence fee to the Town... Upon payment of the animal licence fee, the owner shall be provided with a tag from the Town and shall keep the tag securely fixed on the cat or dog at all times.
dog_limit: No person, being the owner, tenant or occupant of a dwelling unit shall own or harbour, or permit to be kept, owned or harboured more than 2 dogs in or about the dwelling unit.
notes: URL: https://www.whitby.ca/media/j3nnssfo/7294-17_responsible-pet-ownership-by-law_consolidation.pdf. The bylaw does not explicitly define farm dogs, however, the 2-dog limit specifically applies only to a 'dwelling unit', which the bylaw distinctly defines as a suite of rooms 'which is located in a residentially zoned part of the Town'. This effectively exempts agriculturally and rurally zoned properties from the strict dog limit.

collar_tag_req: The Guardian shall securely fix the dog tag on the dog and shall keep such tag securely fixed on the dog at all times until the tag is renewed or replaced.
dog_limit: Residents can have up to three (3) dogs per household.
notes: URL: https://www.citywindsor.ca/documents/city-hall/by-laws-online/by-law%20245-2004.pdf. Dog ownership is also governed by the Keeping of Animals By-law 8156. Standard urban animal control framework with a strict 3-dog limit and no provisions or exemptions for livestock guardian dogs or agricultural working dogs. Dog licensing is transitioning to a voluntary system in 2026, though it remains mandatory for dangerous dogs.

collar_tag_req: All dog owners in Woolwich are required to buy dog tags for each of their dogs annually. When you register your pet with the Township of Woolwich, you will receive a unique licence tag to attach to their collar.
dog_limit: Limit of 3 dogs per household. Keeping 4 or more dogs requires a Kennel Licence.
notes: URL: https://www.woolwich.ca/media/g34gplvw/by-law-31-2018-animal_control_by-law-consolidated_as_of_november-2024_-_current.pdf. Standard animal control by-law. No explicit exemptions or definitions for LGDs or working farm dogs were found.

lgd_definition: “Livestock Guardian Dog” shall mean a dog that works and/or lives with domestic farm animals (e.g. Cattle, Sheep, Poultry) to protect them while repelling predators and is used exclusively for that purpose; (Added by By-law 39-23)
herding_definition: “Herding Dogs” shall mean a dog that has been trained and is actively being used in a bona fide farming operation for the purposes of controlling livestock on the farm; (Added by By-law 39-23)
collar_tag_req: The Township no longer issues municipal dog tags or collects licensing fees for dogs (only kennels). However, the bylaw requires that all dogs within the Township have an identification tag affixed to them containing the dog owner's name and phone number.
dog_limit: In a Dwelling – Single Unit, no person shall, within the Township of Zorra, keep any animal except those permitted in accordance with the following: a) three dogs; b) three domestic cats.
notes: URL: https://www.zorra.ca/media/bg3nti0h/43-15-animal-control-by-law-consolidated-2024-12.pdf. Highly farm-friendly bylaw. The Township recently amended the bylaw in 2023 (By-law 39-23) specifically to add accurate and distinct definitions for both 'Livestock Guardian Dog' and 'Herding Dogs', officially recognizing their working status on bona fide farming operations. The municipality also abolished standard dog licensing fees.
